description: Require that a client request the library accepted can still complete after the node shuts down before any loop dequeues it: the caller's future must either have been responded or carry the node's shutdown channel, so that Error() cannot block forever.

harness.description: TestAssuranceClientFutureShutdownEscape builds a node with background goroutines disabled, BatchApplyCh enabled and a buffered apply channel, calls Apply so the request is accepted, then calls Shutdown and probes the returned future without blocking: it records whether a response is available on the future's channel and whether the future carries the shutdown channel, and reports whether the caller can complete. A control node served by a running loop performs the same call and reports that it completes.
semantic_changes: Conf.skipStartup is set so no loop can dequeue the request, which is what makes an accepted-then-dropped request observable deterministically instead of relying on a shutdown race; Shutdown is called directly on that node.

BatchApplyCh and MaxAppendEntries are set so the apply channel is buffered, which the library documents as a supported option and is the configuration in which a request can be accepted before a loop takes it.
The probe reads the future's own fields non-blockingly rather than calling Error(), which would block; this is a state observation of the mechanism, not a timing observation.
The control uses a single-node cluster with a running loop and a real FSM. No target code is modified.

legality.derivation: S67 shows Error returning from the response channel or from ShutdownCh, so a future with neither cannot complete; S23 shows Apply/ApplyLog/Barrier creating a logFuture and enqueueing it without setting ShutdownCh; S68 shows Shutdown closing the node without draining the apply channel; S11 shows the loops responding only the requests they have taken on. Together they establish both the mechanism and the duty.
legality.applicability: Applies when the request was accepted (the send into the buffered apply channel succeeded) and the node is then shut down before a loop dequeues it.
unresolved: Whether other future types (verifyFuture, configurationChangeFuture, userSnapshotFuture) share the gap.
Whether the maintainers intend completion after Shutdown not to be guaranteed, in which case the correct disposition is a documented caveat rather than an escape.
conflicts: The Future.Error documentation lists ErrRaftShutdown among the errors a caller may see, while the futures returned by Apply/Barrier have no mechanism to produce it once dropped by shutdown.
alternatives: If Shutdown is understood as process end where a blocked caller does not matter, the observation would be a documentation gap only.

grounding.derivation: The obligation requires the accepted request's future to remain completable. The event reports the two ways it could be: a response or the shutdown escape, from the future the library returned.
grounding.applicability: Evaluated only for an accepted request, as declared before the shutdown.

observable_properties.description: An accepted client request has a completion path after the node shuts down: it was responded, or its future carries the shutdown channel.

uncertainties: Whether other future types share the gap.
Whether the maintainers intend no completion guarantee after Shutdown.
The probe observes the mechanism's state rather than blocking in Error(), so it establishes the absence of a completion path rather than the duration of a hang.
